scenes.line1: Ever seen your Go code freeze?
scenes.say: Ever seen your Go program freeze up for no reason? Let's talk about deadlocks and starvation.

scenes.label: Deadlock
scenes.sub: Goroutines wait forever on each other—nothing moves.
scenes.say: A deadlock is when goroutines are stuck waiting on each other forever. Nothing gets done.
Starvation is when some goroutines never get a turn. Maybe one hogs a resource, or others just never run.

scenes.code:
ch := make(chan int)
ch <- 1 // Deadlock: no receiver
scenes.say: Here's a classic deadlock. Sending to a channel with no receiver means your code just hangs.

scenes.question: How do you avoid mutex deadlocks?
scenes.right: Always lock in a consistent order and use defer to unlock right after locking.
scenes.say: Interview trap! If you just say unlock when you're done, that's not enough. Always lock in the same order, and use defer to make sure you always unlock.
